endpoints.description: Every NCR linked to this traveler (any status), in print-ready detail, Event History removed (FR-001/FR-002/FR-003). Fetched by public/javascripts/traveler-print.js in the print page's existing ready handler, the same way the discrepancy log already fetches its own data (research.md R2) — not called server-side by GET /travelers/:id/print, which is unchanged.
endpoints.authentication: Required (session) — auth.ensureAuthenticated, reqUtils.exist('id', Traveler), reqUtils.canReadMw('id') — the same middleware chain GET /travelers/:id/ncr-links/ already uses.

body.sections: Array<Section> — buildNcrPdfModel(ncr, {travelerTitle}).sections with the entry headed 'Event History' removed (research.md R1)

success_200.ordering: The same top-to-bottom order as the inputs each NCR was raised against appear on the traveler's own form (research.md R3) — not creation time. An NCR whose input is no longer on the form sorts after every NCR whose input is still recognized; more than one NCR on the same input keeps its oldest-first relative order (FR-010).
success_200.empty_case: [] when the traveler has no linked NCRs — the client renders a 'no NCRs' line (FR-005) rather than leaving the section blank

notes: Query: lib/traveler-ncr.js#findAllLinkedNcrs(travelerId) — same traveler_link filter GET /travelers/:id/ncr-links/ already uses, minus its status filter, full documents (no projection), sorted oldest-first as a baseline.

Ordering: lib/traveler-ncr.js#orderNcrsByFormPosition(ncrs, activeFormLabels(traveler)) re-sorts that baseline by each NCR's linked input's position on the traveler's active form (research.md R3) — the actual order returned to the client.

Every value inside a Section is already a plain string (lib/ncr-pdf.js's own text()/formatDate()) — the client never does date math or null-handling, only inserts strings via .text() (research.md R5).

endpoints.description: The traveler's own complete review/approval history (FR-006/FR-007), reviewer ids resolved to names. Fetched by public/javascripts/traveler-print.js alongside ncr-print-details/, in the same ready handler.
endpoints.authentication: Required (session) — same middleware chain as ncr-print-details/ above.

body.heading: 'Approvals'
body.table_or_note: { table: { head: ['Reviewer','Outcome','Date','Comments'], rows: Array<[String,String,String,String]>, widths: [3,2,2,4] } } when there is at least one recorded result, else { note: 'None recorded' }

success_200.note_on_shape: A single Section object (research.md R1's Section shape), not an array — pre-wrapped server-side so the client can pass this endpoint's response straight to the same renderSection(container, section) call used for each ncr-print-details/ entry, with no client-side reshaping (revised from an earlier draft of this contract, which had the client build the table itself).
success_200.ordering: The order the results were recorded in (traveler.__review.reviewResults' own order) — every recorded result, not filtered to current-version/non-voided only (research.md R4)
success_200.empty_case: { heading: 'Approvals', note: 'None recorded' } when the traveler has no review history (FR-007)

notes: Resolution: one batched User.find({_id: {$in: [...uniqueReviewerIds]}}, 'name').lean() call, then lib/traveler-ncr.js#reviewRecordRows(traveler, reviewerNames) (research.md R4) — the same reviewer-name-resolution pattern routes/form.js already uses for a Form's own review results; routes/traveler.js never did this for travelers before this feature.

Wrapping: lib/ncr-pdf.js#tableSection('Approvals', ['Reviewer','Outcome','Date','Comments'], rows, [3,2,2,4]) — tableSection is now exported from lib/ncr-pdf.js (it already existed there, used internally by buildNcrPdfModel; this feature is its first external caller) so the empty-rows-becomes-a-note behaviour is not re-implemented a second time.
__review.policy is never returned: allApproved() does not actually read it, so surfacing it would misrepresent how the traveler was really approved.

Section.note: The existing shape lib/ncr-pdf.js#buildNcrPdfModel already produces — reused as-is, not redefined by this feature.
variants: { heading: String, table: { head: Array<String>, rows: Array<Array<String>>, widths?: Array<Number> } }

client_contract.fetches: Both endpoints above, in the existing $(function() {...}) ready handler, alongside the discrepancy log's own existing fetch.
client_contract.render_targets: views/traveler-print.jade gains two empty containers, #ncr-print-sections and #review-records. A small local renderSection(container, section) function (research.md R5) draws one Section into one container; #review-records gets exactly one call (the single Section the review-records/ endpoint already returns), #ncr-print-sections gets one call per ncr-print-details/ entry (preceded by that entry's own ncrTitle as a sub-heading) — no client-side reshaping of either response, only drawing.
client_contract.escaping: Every Section value is inserted via jQuery .text() (or an equivalent safe DOM-building call), never .html() or a template-string built from a value — this is what satisfies FR-009 (no NCR/review free text is ever interpreted as markup) on the client, since there is no server-side auto-escaping step for this content.
client_contract.print_gating: #create-pdf stays disabled until both fetches above have resolved (research.md R7) — ensures the one existing print action (FR-008) always produces a complete record (FR-001/FR-006) rather than racing the user's click.
